messages:
rachel: quick morning sync 1: exploring SNR-style probes to distinguish warmups from abusive bursts. want tradeoffs documented before coding.

tom: +1. clarify SNR: ratio of useful traffic (cache hits, low latency) to noisy traffic. need cheap proxies for 'useful'.

vikram: idea: compute mini-signals at edge: cache_hit_hint (0/1), avg_tokens_per_req, distinct_prompt_hashes/min. combine into a single burstiness_score. if score low but rps high -> suspect abuse.

emily: ops concern: keep metric cardinality low. emit tenant.burstiness.min, tenant.cache_hint.rate per minute. avoid per-request tags.

rachel: enforcement path: soft-deny via delayed ack + lower priority queue vs hard deny. soft-deny lowers concurrency and applies small probability drops; hard deny kicks in for sustained badness.

tom: config snippet (proto):
{"policy":"snr-probe-v1","burst_threshold":0.7,"probe_fraction":0.01,"soft_drop_pct":0.15,"sustain_window_mins":5}

vikram: sampling probes into ML is useful but expensive. run probes at 1% for PLG, 0% for enterprise by default, opt-in via control plane.

emily: runbook: when tenant.burstiness > threshold for 10m, page on-call with severity low; include cached sample of probe metrics and recent token usage.

ops-bot: reminder: deploy freeze Thu 02:00-06:00 UTC. avoid major policy flips then.

rachel: next steps: I'll draft a focused RFC with signal definitions, policy schema, and rollout plan. small canary first. meeting 9am tomorrow to review.
